newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL NOON RUBBER FIRM BUT DEALERS WATCH RUPIAH.
newsitem.headline: KL NOON RUBBER FIRM BUT DEALERS WATCH RUPIAH.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were firm at Thursday noon but dealers said they expected the market to soften later this week or even next based on the weakness of the Indonesian rupiah.
Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, said on Thursday it will no longer announce its daily intervention and conversion bands for the rupiah, effectively floating the currency.
The rupiah plunged to a new low against the dollar.
Indonesian rubber prices were not immediately affected by the news, but dealers said the market could come up under pressure eventually from buyers expecting cheaper prices.
"If the rubber price keeps falling in Indonesia, we may have no choice but to match it," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur.
"As it is, there is very little demand in the region, and we cannot be selling higher than others."
At midday, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the RSS1 for September buyer at 250 cents (90 U.S. cents) a kg, up half cent from Wednesday's close.
The SMR20 for September buyer was unchanged at 248.50.
For Aug/Sept, trading houses were offering the SMR 20 at 247 cents a kg, the SMR CV at 289 cents, SMR L at 272, SMR 5 at 262, SMR 10 at 248 and drum latex at 190.
Dealers said the market was positive because of the weak ringgit against the U.S. dollar, although there was hardly any buying going on.
They said it was difficult to say how long the uptrend could last. "We may have to make the adjustments from tomorrow or even next week," said one dealer.
The ringgit was at 2.7760 to a dollar in Kuala Lumpur at 0500 GMT, after opening at 2.7580 at 0200 GMT.
